source.title: Paper Replication Walkthrough: Reverse-Engineering Modular Addition

record.file_problem: None; the supplied post text is coherent, but summarizes linked walkthroughs rather than including them.
record.tranche_reason: The post explicitly describes a replication of the author's grokking paper, including training a modular-addition model and examining its circuits during training.
record.gate_note: The post reports results only in a brief summary. The linked videos and notebook are not included here. It does not give accuracy values, a training-set-size comparison, or specific circuit-removal results.
record.test_reason: The post announces a coding replication of the authors' own 'Progress Measures' paper (an original source), with a modular-addition model that 'does grok'. The post itself gives no numbers, curves or circuit results. Those are in linked videos and a notebook that were not supplied. It amounts to a self-replication by the original authors, reported only as a qualitative summary.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it should be framed as an announcement. The post presents a three-part video and code walkthrough replicating the Progress Measures paper. The authors train a modular-addition model that groks, reverse-engineer its trig-based circuit, and use progress measures to watch the circuits develop and explain why it groks. It presents no data itself.
record.recipe_differences: Described as a coding walkthrough replicating the author's paper, but the supplied post does not specify the training setup or establish that every method detail matches.
record.problems: The supplied post is a brief overview rather than the walkthrough or paper; it provides no quantitative performance or timing details and no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Size and timing of the train/test delay; the dependence of the delay on training-set size.

All quantitative parts: gradual Fourier-circuit formation, later removal of memorizing components, and progress measures anticipating the jump. Any results exist only in the unseen videos and notebook.

missing.what: Accuracy curves, progress-measure trajectories and circuit analyses from the actual walkthrough
missing.locator: Linked videos (neelnanda.io/modular-addition-walkthrough-1/2/3) and notebook (neelnanda.io/modular-addition-notebook); not in the supplied text

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given. The post contains no readable results, and it is the original V2 source's authors replicating their own paper, so it is not independent evidence. The reader's 'supports' labels for V1 and V2 rest on one-sentence summaries and are removed. Possibly better classed as 'discusses' if the linked material stays unavailable.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report accuracy values or the delay between training and test performance, nor whether the delay changes with training-set size.

The post does not specify the timing or detailed results of circuit formation, whether memorizing components are removed later, or quantitative evidence that the progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.

rows.subject: a model
rows.operation_detail: Train a model on modular addition and report that it groks.
rows.measure: Grokking outcome; the post says the model groks, without specifying an accuracy trajectory.
rows.value: The post says the model does grok.
rows.note: No numerical accuracy, timing, or training-set-size comparison is provided.
rows.check: The only evidence is the sentence 'see that it does grok'. There is no accuracy trajectory, no train/test delay and no training-set-size comparison, so the extent of the effect can't be read. 'Partial' implies a measured weaker effect, which isn't there.

rows.subject: the model
rows.operation_detail: Use progress measures to distinguish progress toward generalizing and memorizing algorithms, then inspect circuit development during training.
rows.measure: Progress measures for the generalizing and memorizing algorithms and circuit development.
rows.value: The post says the measures distinguish progress toward the two algorithms and that the circuits are examined as they develop to understand grokking.
rows.note: No specific progress values, timing, or later removal of memorizing components is stated.
rows.check: The post only says progress measures were defined and that circuits were watched during training. No results are reported on gradual formation, later removal of memorization, or anticipation of the jump. It is also a replication by the original source's own authors.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
